subject: Supply chain MAP: staggered GPU pool plan & evaluation timeline

Subject: Supply chain MAP: staggered GPU pool plan & evaluation timeline

Kyle —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, I attached a draft mutual action plan that lays out a staggered reservation approach to match Pioneer Health's compliance and go-live milestones while reducing upfront spend. High level notes in the doc:

- Phase A (POC/eval): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized) for 4 weeks; prioritized for latency-sensitive prompts.
- Phase B (pilot): scale to 12x GPUs with burstable capacity to 20x for 8 weeks.
- Phase C (prod reserve): committed 24x GPU pool with regional redundancy (primary us-east, fallback us-west).

Key asks from Pioneer: target latency under 150ms p95 for your core inference path, and SOC2 evidence for data handling during the eval. We included a 6-week lead time to provision private Dedicated capacity in the MAP because of current supply projections with our partner.

I noted two open items we promised to follow up on: exact prompt length distributions (you mentioned typical 256 tokens, occasional 1k spikes) and confirmation on whether pilot traffic can tolerate a 10% early-error fallback window.

I've copied Karthik and Marissa to add sizing equations and procurement notes; we'll also loop NovaCloud if we have to accelerate physical capacity.

Next steps:
1) Review attached MAP and sizing workbook — please comment with redlines by Wed 5/13.
2) I'll book a 30-min follow-up on Thurs 5/14 to walk the timeline and acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Camila —

Thanks for the quick docs. Couple of clarifying Qs for the MAP so we can align with procurement: 

1) That 6-week lead time for private Dedicated — is that an average or worst-case with your partners? We may need to bump ceilings for regulatory timelines.
2) For Phase A eval, can we start with burst credits on hosted API while Dedicated is being provisioned, to avoid blocking engineering?
3) Do you have a short checklist of the SOC2 evidence items you can entregate quickly? Procurement asked for the minimal package to get a PO in flight.

I'll review the sizing sheet with our infra lead tomorrow and get you concrete prompt-distribution numbers by EOD Monday. If procurement is involved we'll need a simple payment / PO cadence captured in the MAP.

Subject: RE: Supply chain MAP: staggered GPU pool plan & evaluation timeline

Kyle —

Quick answers below, pulling from the sizing workbook attached: RDW uses a partner-mixed supply model for Dedicated Private installs. Current realistic provisioning lead time to stand up a committed 24x pool in a single region is 5-8 weeks (we quoted conservatively at 6 weeks in the MAP). Worst-case (hardware delays + regulatory network approvals) could push to 10 weeks — we call that out as an escalation path.

About your other points:
- Hosted API burst credits: yes. We can provide hosted burst capacity for the earliest parts of Phase A while Dedicated capacity is being brought up. We will put explicit quotas and a migration runbook in the eval-runbook.md attachment.
- SOC2 evidence: attached is a minimal artifact list we can hand to procurement (SOC2 report PDF, architecture diagram with data flow, data retention policy excerpt). We can redact customer-specific telemetry if needed.
- PO cadence: typical is monthly billing for hosted bursts + a prepay/commit schedule for Dedicated; procurement prefers net-30 on committed contracts. We can mirror that in the MAP payment appendix.

Sizing note (short): with 256 token average and p95 latency target 150ms, estimated steady-state tokens/s maps to ~0.6 A100-eq per 100 concurrent prompt workers after quantization and KV-cache. For your target pilot throughput (approx 2.5k concurrent workers), that suggests ~15 A100-equivalents before burst. We included a safety margin to reach 20 for pilot bursts. See gpu_pool_sizing_model.xlsx for the math.

I'll join Monday's sync if helpful.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: evaluation-runbook.md, minimal-soc2-package.pdf

Thanks for the details. A few procurement-specific asks so we can move a PO: 

- Can you provide a draft SOW or commitment appendix that lays out phases A/B/C with acceptance criteria we can attach to the PO? We prefer an exhibit with clear gating tests.
- If Dedicated lead-time stretches beyond 8 weeks, will Redwood provide credits or pro-rated refunds for missed SLAs on provisioning?
- Please confirm invoicing entity and where to send the PO (billing@redwood.com?) and whether Redwood accepts net-30 on committed capacity.

We aim to have an internal decision by 5/21; the MAP timeline will help. Procurement has reviewed the SOC2 artifacts and asked only for the certificate scan — that looked fine.

Thanks — very helpful questions. I'm attaching an SOW appendix template that outlines gating criteria per phase and a proposed provisioning SLA for Dedicated lead time. Points below: 

- Draft SOW appendix: describes acceptance tests (latency p95 under 150ms across 1k sampled requests, model-quality pass-rate on your eval set at >= 92%, and successful hot failover between us-east/us-west).
- Lead-time credit: we propose a service credit equal to 5% of the monthly committed fee for each full week of missed provisioning beyond 8 weeks, capped at 25%. This is in the provisioning SLA clause in the appendix; we can adjust language per legal review.
- Invoicing: please send PO to billing@redwood.com. We accept net-30 for committed capacity; hosted bursts billed monthly.
